answer: Time-locked stake bonding curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock tokens in an escrow contract that slashes deposits upon cryptographic proof of equivocation. Rather than leaving reputation as mere fable, it binds each key to a scarce pearl of capital so bots cannot hollow out consensus like porous karst. Attackers incur locked liquidity and opportunity costs per identity. However, wealthy adversaries can still fund Sybil fleets when exploit gains exceed borrowing costs.
